cook.role-group-empty: `{Written}` opens brackets and names no {What}. Write one - `{Example}` - or drop the brackets.
cook.role-space-not-text: `{Written}` has a second name in its brackets, and `asset` takes only a kind. A namespace is a `text` thing - the folders an asset is looked for in come from the recipe, keyed by the kind.
cook.role-space-empty: `{Written}` ends in a comma and names no namespace. Write one - `text(Achievement,Quests)` - or drop the comma.
cook.array-gap: `{Table}.{Group}` leaves element {Element} empty while a later element has a value. An array with a gap in it reads as one whose middle holds the type's empty value, which a consumer cannot tell from a value that was written. Fill it, move the later values up, or set `AllowArrayGaps` on the source entry.
cook.required-in-object-outside-object: `{Table}.{Field}` has no value, and the sheet marks the column as required. It is marked required inside an object and is not part of one, which reads as required.
cook.record-member-required-empty: `{Table}.{Group}` element {Element} exists and its `{Member}` is empty, which the sheet marks as required inside the object. Give it a value, or clear the rest of the element so that there is no record here.
cook.required-empty: `{Table}.{Field}` has no value, and the sheet declares the column required. Write one, or type the column `{Type}?` so that a row may say it has none.
cook.asset-no-roots: {Columns} column(s) are typed `asset` and no folders are configured to check them against, so nothing was checked. Name the folders in the recipe's `Assets.Roots` to switch the check on.
cook.asset-no-folder-without-kind: `{Table}.{Field}` is typed `asset`, and the recipe configures no folder for a column without a kind. Configured: {Configured}.
cook.asset-no-folder-for-kind: `{Table}.{Field}` is typed `asset({Kind})`, and the recipe configures no folder for kind `{Kind}`. Configured: {Configured}.
cook.index-type-unusable: Index field `{Table}.{Field}` is `{Type}`, {Why} Use a whole-number, string, uuid or enum column as an index.
cook.index-optional: Index field `{Table}.{Field}` cannot be optional: drop the `?` from its type, because every row must have a value for an index.
cook.index-duplicate: Index field `{Table}.{Field}` repeats the value `{Value}`, first used at {First}. Values in an index field must be unique.
cook.index-absent: `{Table}.{Field}` identifies the row, and this row says it has no value there. Write one: an index cannot be absent.
cook.reference-enum-key: `{Table}.{Field}` references `{Target}`, whose index is an enum. Every other key type can be referenced; this one cannot yet, because an enum travels in an encoding of its own and the generated readers have no call for it here. Key `{Target}` by the enum's underlying `int`, or carry the value here as that enum and look the row up through `{Target}`'s own index.
cook.reference-blank: Field `{Table}.{Field}` references `{Target}` and this row leaves the cell empty. Write the key of a row to point at, or `-` to say this row points at none.
cook.reference-none-but-required: Field `{Table}.{Field}` references `{Target}` and this row says it points at none, but the column is declared required. Give it a row to point at, or declare the column optional.
cook.reference-missing-row: Field `{Table}.{Field}` references `{Target}` row `{Value}`, which does not exist.
cook.reference-excluded-by-side: In a `{Side}` build, field `{Table}.{Field}` references table `{Target}`, which that build excludes by target side.
cook.reference-key-unparsable: `{Table}.{Field}` references `{Targets}`, which is addressed by `{KeyType}`, and `{Written}` is not one. {Detail}
cook.reference-table-missing: Field `{Table}.{Field}` references table `{Target}`, which does not exist.
cook.reference-field-of-own-table: Field `{Table}.{Field}` references `{Table}.{RefField}`, which is a field of its own table. A reference that names a field is followed, so this one begins a loop.
cook.reference-field-missing: Field `{Table}.{Field}` references `{RefTable}.{RefField}`, but table `{Resolved}` has no field named `{RefField}`.
cook.reference-cycle: A cyclic reference has been detected while resolving `{Table}.{Field}`. The chain returns to `{Returns}`.
cook.record-reference-names-field: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` member `{Field}` references the field `{RefField}` rather than a whole row. A reference inside a record must name the table alone. Drop the `.{RefField}`, or move the column out of the group.
cook.multi-target-id-overlap: `{Table}.{Field}` may be a row of `{First}` or of `{Second}`, and both hold `{Shared}`. An id in two of them makes the generated accessors answer together, and which row the column meant is then not in the data. Give the two tables separate id bands, or point at them from separate columns.
cook.multi-target-missing-row: `{Table}.{Field}` holds `{Value}`, which is not a row of `{Targets}`.
cook.multi-target-keys-differ: Field `{Table}.{Field}` references `{Targets}`, and they are not keyed alike - the column holds one value and would have to be `{KeyTypes}` at once. Key them the same way, or point at them from separate columns.
cook.multi-target-enum-name-taken: `{Table}.{Field}` reaches several tables, so the generated code needs an enum named `{Enum}` to say which one - and an enum of that name is already declared. Rename one of them.
cook.value-not-allowed: `{Table}.{Field}` is `{Value}`, which the column's list of allowed values does not name. Allowed: {Allowed}.
cook.element-value-not-allowed: `{Table}.{Field}` (element {Element}) is `{Value}`, which the column's list of allowed values does not name. Allowed: {Allowed}.
cook.value-below-minimum: `{Table}.{Field}` is {Value}, below the minimum {Minimum} the column declares.
cook.element-value-below-minimum: `{Table}.{Field}` (element {Element}) is {Value}, below the minimum {Minimum} the column declares.
cook.value-above-maximum: `{Table}.{Field}` is {Value}, above the maximum {Maximum} the column declares.
cook.element-value-above-maximum: `{Table}.{Field}` (element {Element}) is {Value}, above the maximum {Maximum} the column declares.
cook.row-set-owner-missing: `{Set}` names another set of `{Owner}`'s rows, which this run does not have. A name matching `TableRowSets` contributes rows to a table rather than declaring one, so the table has to be there - check the spelling, or that the source holding it is not excluded.
cook.row-set-columns-differ: `{Set}` and `{Owner}` are two sets of one table's rows, so `{Owner}` has to declare every column `{Set}` holds. {Difference}
cook.invalid-identifier: `{Name}` is not a valid identifier, so it cannot name a field or an entity. A name has to start with a letter or underscore and hold only letters, digits and underscores.
cook.unrecognized-type-question-mark: type `{Type}` is an unrecognized type. A `?` goes after the type or after the brackets: `int?` says a row may have no value, `int?[]` says an element may, and `int?[]?` says both.
cook.type-takes-no-brackets: type `{Type}` names something in brackets, but `{Bare}` is not a type that takes one. `text` takes a group and `asset` takes a kind.
cook.type-not-array-element: type `{Type}` cannot be used as an array element.
cook.formula-error: Cell contains the formula error `{Error}`. Fix the formula, or replace it with a literal value. The source entry's `OnFormulaError: "empty"` reads cells like this as empty instead, for a workbook this run does not own.
cook.blank-cell-required: This cell is empty, and a value of type `{Type}` belongs here. Write one, declare the column optional and write `-` to say this row has no value, or - for sheets this project cannot correct - read blanks as the type's empty value with the source entry's `OnBlankCell: "empty"`.
cook.blank-cell-optional: This cell is empty, and a value of type `{Type}` belongs here. Write one, write `-` to say this row has no value, or - for sheets this project cannot correct - read blanks as the type's empty value with the source entry's `OnBlankCell: "empty"`.
cook.value-unparsable: Cannot parse `{Written}` as a value of type `{Type}`. ({Detail})
cook.not-a-boolean: `{Value}` is not a boolean. Use Y/N, YES/NO, TRUE/FALSE, 1/0, or leave the cell empty for false.
cook.array-element-no-value-mark: Element {Element} of this cell is `{Mark}`, which says it has no value - and this column's elements are required. Write a value, mark the elements optional by writing the `?` inside the brackets as in `int?[]`, or write `{Escaped}` for the character itself.
cook.time-in-dst-gap: `{Time}` is a time that does not exist in `{Zone}` - the clocks there jumped over it when daylight saving began. Write a time on either side of the gap, or set the entry's `TimeZone` to a fixed offset such as `+09:00`, which has no gaps.
cook.magnitude-too-large: `{Text}` does not fit a signed 64-bit value, and `{Type}` is a magnitude. A value that uses all 64 bits belongs in a `bitset` column.
cook.float-loses-exactness: `{Text}` is above what `{Type}` holds exactly ({Exact}), so it would read back as a different value.
cook.radix-too-many-digits: `{Text}` carries {Digits} base-{Radix} digits, and 64 bits take at most {Limit}.
cook.radix-bad-digit: `{Text}` has `{Digit}` where a base-{Radix} digit belongs.
cook.bitset-empty: a `bitset` cell is empty. Write a value, or type the column `bitset?` to say a blank is expected.
cook.bitset-signed: `{Text}` carries a sign, and a `bitset` holds a bit pattern rather than a magnitude. Every bit set is `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`.
cook.bitset-decimal-point: `{Text}` has a decimal point, and a flag set has no fractional part. `1.0` is refused with `1.5`, so that neither has to be guessed at.
cook.bitset-thousands-separator: `{Text}` has a thousands separator, which says nothing about a bit pattern.
cook.bitset-exponent: `{Text}` is in exponent notation, which a `bitset` does not read. Write `0x…` or `0b…`.
cook.bitset-digit-separator: `{Text}` has a digit separator, which this notation does not take.
cook.bitset-not-a-digit: `{Text}` has `{Character}` where a decimal digit belongs. A base-16 or base-2 value is written `0x…` or `0b…`.
cook.bitset-above-2-53: `{Text}` is above 2^53, where a spreadsheet's numeric cell has already lost the exact value. Write it as `0x…` or `0b…`.
cook.notice-formula-error-empty: `{Column}` holds cells whose formula is an error, read as the type's empty value because the source entry sets `OnFormulaError: "empty"`.
cook.notice-blank-filled: `{Column}` holds cells nobody filled in, read as the type's empty value because the source entry sets `OnBlankCell: "empty"`.
cook.notice-blank-is-empty-value: `{Column}` holds blank cells, which are now the type's empty value rather than "no value". Write `-` in the rows that have none.
cook.notice-ambiguous-time: Cells hold a time that occurs twice in `{Zone}`, where daylight saving ends, read as the standard-time one. Write the offset in the cell, as `2022-11-06T01:30:00-04:00`, for the other.
recipe.array-delimiter-not-one-character: Recipe setting `ArrayDelimiter` is `{Delimiter}`, but it must be exactly one character.
recipe.row-sets-conflicting-patterns: Two source entries declare different `TableRowSets` patterns: {Patterns}. Table names are shared across the whole run, so one pattern has to describe all of them.
recipe.row-sets-bad-regex: `TableRowSets` is `{Pattern}`, which is not a regular expression: {Detail}
recipe.row-sets-missing-groups: `TableRowSets` is `{Pattern}`, which needs a `{TableGroup}` group naming the table and a `{SetGroup}` group naming the set - for example `^(?<{TableGroup}>.+?)(?<{SetGroup}>_alt)$`.
recipe.entry-array-delimiter-not-one-cha: Recipe `{Section}` sets `ArrayDelimiter` to `{Value}`, but it must be exactly one character.
recipe.on-blank-cell-unknown: Recipe `{Section}` sets `OnBlankCell` to `{Value}`. It takes `error` or `empty`.
recipe.on-formula-error-unknown: Recipe `{Section}` sets `OnFormulaError` to `{Value}`. It takes `error` or `empty`.
recipe.on-duplicate-index-unknown: Recipe `{Section}` sets `OnDuplicateIndex` to `{Value}`. It takes `error`, `keep-first` or `keep-last`.
recipe.workbook-pattern-has-sheet: Recipe `{Section}` has `{Text}` in `{Key}`, which reads as a workbook and a sheet. This list is about workbooks alone, so write the workbook without the brackets; `[workbook]sheet` belongs in `IncludeSheets` or `ExcludeSheets`.
recipe.sheet-pattern-unclosed-bracket: Recipe `{Section}` has `{Text}` in `{Key}`, which opens a workbook name with `[` and never closes it. The form is `[workbook]sheet`.
recipe.sheet-pattern-no-workbook: Recipe `{Section}` has `{Text}` in `{Key}`, which names no workbook between its brackets. Leave the brackets off for a pattern that applies to every workbook.
recipe.sheet-pattern-no-sheet: Recipe `{Section}` has `{Text}` in `{Key}`, which names a workbook and no sheet. Use `{Alternative}Workbooks` for a whole workbook.
recipe.google-key-file-and-variable: Recipe section `{Section}` names both `ServiceAccountKeyFile` and `ServiceAccountKeyVariable`. Name one: the file for a key on disk, the variable for one held in a secret store.
recipe.google-service-account-and-client: Recipe section `{Section}` names both a service account key and `ClientSecretFilename`. Those authenticate as different identities, so name one: the service account for an unattended run, the client secret for a person at a machine.
recipe.google-no-credential: Recipe section `{Section}` names no credential. Set `ServiceAccountKeyFile` or `ServiceAccountKeyVariable` for an unattended run, or `ClientSecretFilename` to authenticate as the person running it.
recipe.assets-on-missing-unknown: Recipe setting `Assets.OnMissing` is `{Value}`. It has to be `warn`, `error` or `ignore`.
recipe.assets-root-missing: `Assets.Roots` points at `{Path}`, and there is no folder at `{Full}`. A root that is not there is a recipe mistake rather than a tree with nothing in it - every value checked against it would be reported missing.
recipe.data-file-case-unknown: The recipe sets `DataFileCase` to `{Value}`. It takes `pascal`, `camel`, `snake` or `upper-snake`, or nothing at all to name each data file after its table.
recipe.naming-case-unknown: Recipe `Naming` sets `{Key}` to `{Value}`. It takes `pascal`, `camel`, `snake` or `upper-snake`.
recipe.naming-on-violation-unknown: Recipe `Naming` sets `OnViolation` to `{Value}`. It takes `error` or `warn`. To leave a kind of name unchecked, leave its spelling blank instead.
recipe.naming-severity-unknown: Recipe `Naming` sets `{Key}` to `{Value}`. It takes `error`, `warn` or `ignore`.
recipe.row-sets-group-captured-other-tab: `TableRowSets` matches `{Set}` but its `{TableGroup}` group captured `{Captured}`, so the pattern does not say which table this is a set of rows for.
recipe.layout-unknown: A recipe source asks for the sheet layout `{Layout}`, which does not exist. Use one of: {Known}.
recipe.history-no-project-key: Recipe `{Section}` records history but names no ProjectKey. One database can hold several projects and they are told apart by it.
recipe.history-on-failure-unknown: Recipe `{Section}` sets OnFailure to `{Value}`, which is not a value. Use `warn` or `fail`.
recipe.summary-author-unknown: The summary target sets `Author` to `{Value}`. It takes `full`, `masked` or `none`.
cook.type-has-no-empty-value: There is no empty value for type `{Type}`, so a column of it cannot be optional.
cook.index-type-unusable-in-table: The index field `{Field}` is `{Type}`, {Why} Use a whole-number, string, uuid or enum column as the index.
cook.index-field-optional: The index field cannot be optional: `int?` is not allowed for the index field, because every row must have an index.
cook.index-field-target-side: The target-side of the index field must be set to CS.
cook.wire-tag-on-serial-member: Field `{Table}.{Field}` is part of the serial field `{Serial}` and carries wire tag {Tag}. A serial field is one column on the wire, so the tag goes on its first member only.
cook.wire-tag-only-on-tombstone: Table `{Table}` has a `#`-excluded column reserving a wire tag, but no live field carries one. Tags are all-or-none per table: give every field its `@N`, or drop the tag from the tombstone.
cook.wire-tags-partial: Table `{Table}` tags some fields and not others: {Untagged} carry no `@N`. Tags are all-or-none per table, because a half-tagged table gets neither mode's guarantees.
cook.wire-tag-reused: Field `{Table}.{Field}` declares wire tag {Tag}, which {Holder} already holds. A tag identifies a column for the life of the data, so it can never be shared or reused.
validate.rule-has-no-entry: [{File}] has nothing to run. A rule file is a class with `public static void {Entry}({Context} context)`, and the context is how it reports. Helpers with no entry belong in `{SharedPath}/`, which is compiled with every rule but never run on its own.
validate.rule-entry-declared-twice: [{File}] declares `{Entry}()` more than once, so which one is the rule is not decided. Keep one and call the rest from it.
validate.rule-entry-wrong-context: [{File}] declares `{Owner}.{Entry}` but it does not take a `{Context}`, which is what `{Folder}/` hands over. Write `public static void {Entry}({Context} context)`. A rule moved here from another stage takes the other stage's context, and the two differ in what they carry.
validate.reports-over-cap: [{File}] made {Extra} more report(s) than the {Shown} shown. A rule reporting this much is usually the rule being wrong rather than the data.
validate.table-rule-unnamed: [{File}] does not say which table it is for. A table rule is named `<table>{Suffix}.cs` - rename it to `{Name}{Suffix}.cs` if it is the rule for `{Name}`.
validate.table-rule-orphaned: [{File}] is a rule for table `{Table}`, which this model does not have.{Hint} Rename the file to follow the table, or move its checks into `{GlobalFolder}/` if they are not about one table.
validate.table-rule-declares-tier: [{File}] declares a tier, which `{TableFolder}/` has no use for: its rules run at the same time as each other and each is about one table. Move the checks into `{GlobalFolder}/` if their order matters, or drop the attribute.
validate.tier-unreadable: [{File}] declares a tier this cannot read. Write a plain number - the tiers are settled before any rule is compiled, so a named constant is not available to read here.
validate.no-rule-files: The validation folder `{Root}` holds no rule files. Put `.cs` files in `{TableFolder}/`, `{GlobalFolder}/`, `{RuntimeFolder}/` or `{PreFolder}/` - or clear `Validation.Path` to run without validation.
validate.tables-before-sheets-read: This rule reads `Tables` through the context, which holds nothing before the sheets are read. Move it out of `{PreFolder}/` - the tables exist from `{TableFolder}/` onward.
validate.schema-before-sheets-read: This rule reads `Schema`, which is not available before the sheets are read. Move it out of `{PreFolder}/` - the tables exist from `{TableFolder}/` onward.
validate.option-not-set: This rule reads the validation option `{Key}`, which the recipe does not set. Add it under `Validation.Options` ({Known}).
validate.store-outside-runtime-stage: This rule opens an external store, which only the `{RuntimeFolder}/` rules may do. Move the file there - it is the folder `--skip-runtime-validation` can leave out, and that only works if the rules that need a store are in it.
validate.files-needs-folder: `Files()` needs a folder to scan. Pass one - `Option("ContentRoot")` is where it usually comes from.
validate.files-folder-missing: `Files("{Root}", "{Pattern}")` found no folder at `{Full}`. A rule that checks assets needs the content root, which the recipe passes through `Validation.Options`.
validate.path-folder-missing: The recipe's `Validation.Path` is `{Path}`, which resolves to `{Root}` - and there is no folder there. Create it with the `{RulesFolder}/pre/` `{RulesFolder}/tables/` `{RulesFolder}/global/` `{RulesFolder}/runtime/` layout, or clear `Validation.Path` to run without validation.
validate.unknown-subfolder: `{Parent}` has a subfolder `{Name}`, which is not one this layout runs. {Advice} - or prefix it with `#` to have it skipped.
validate.stage-at-root: The validation folder `{Root}` has {Stray} at its root, which is where the stages were before they moved under `{RulesFolder}/`. Move it there - the rules themselves need no change.
validate.stages-at-root: The validation folder `{Root}` has {Stray} at its root, which is where the stages were before they moved under `{RulesFolder}/`. Move them there - the rules themselves need no change.
validate.no-path-for-new-rule: The recipe has no `Validation.Path`, so there is no folder to put a rule in. Set it to where the rules should live - beside the sheets is the usual place.
validate.new-validator-needs-table: `--new-validator` needs the name of the table to write a rule for.
validate.rule-file-exists: `{Path}` already exists. Open it rather than starting it again - a rule file is somebody's work, and this command will not overwrite one.
validate.store-not-a-query: Validation may only read: `{Head}` is not a query. Use SELECT, WITH or SHOW.
validate.connection-not-a-database: `Validation.Connections.{Name}` names the scheme `{Scheme}:`, which `Db()` does not open. Use `mysql:` or `postgres:` - or `Redis("{Name}")` if it is a cache.
validate.connection-not-redis: `Validation.Connections.{Name}` names the scheme `{Scheme}:`, which `Redis()` does not open. Use `redis://host:port/db`, or `Db("{Name}")` if it is a database.
validate.connection-not-configured: This rule opens the connection `{Name}`, which the recipe does not have. Add it under `Validation.Connections` ({Known}).
validate.connection-no-scheme: `Validation.Connections.{Name}` does not say which kind of store it is. Begin it with `mysql:`, `postgres:` or `redis://`.
cook.constant-not-found: constant `{Name}` was not found in the constant-set `{Set}`
cook.enum-label-not-found: Label '{Label}' was not found in the enum '{Enum}'
cook.enum-value-not-found: Value '{Value}' was not found in the enum '{Enum}'
cook.field-is-not-an-enum: Field `{Table}.{Field}` has type `{Type}`, which is not an enum.
cook.array-mixes-types: Array `{Table}.{Group}` mixes types: element {FirstElement} is `{FirstType}` and element {Element} is `{Type}`. Every element of an array is the same type.
cook.record-level-is-value-and-record: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` uses `{Member}` as both a value and a record: `{Ends}` ends there where `{Deeper}` goes further in. A level is one or the other.
cook.record-numbers-two-levels: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` puts its element number in two places: `{Shape}` numbers a different level than `{Other}`. `name["Member"][0]` is one record whose members are arrays and `name[0]["Member"]` is an array of records; a group is one or the other.
cook.record-numbers-too-many-levels: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` numbers {Count} of its levels in `{Shape}`. One level of a group holds the element number; an array nested inside another array is only supported where the inner level has no name of its own, as in `Grid1{Separator}2`.
cook.record-numbers-inner-and-nests: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` numbers a level inside itself and also nests: member `{Member}` is a record, and the element number is not on `{Group}`. Number the group instead - `{Group}1{Separator}{Member}{Separator}{Inner}`.
cook.record-numbered-level-references: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` numbers its inner level rather than naming it, and element {Element} references another table. A reference needs a name to keep its key under. Name the level - `{Group}{Separator}<name>` - or carry the key as a plain `int`.
cook.record-member-element-counts-differ: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` has {FirstCount} element(s) for member `{First}` but {Count} for `{Member}`. Every element of a record must declare every member.
cook.record-numbered-inconsistently: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` is numbered inconsistently: member `{First}` has element {FirstElement} where `{Member}` has {Element}. Every member must use the same element numbers.
cook.record-member-types-differ: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` member `{Member}` has type `{FirstType}` at element {FirstElement} and `{Type}` at element {Element}. Every element of a member must have the same type - the file stores the member as one column and states one type for it.
cook.record-mixes-target-sides: Record group `{Table}.{Group}` mixes target sides: `{First}` is `{FirstSide}` and `{Member}` is `{Side}`. A record is included in a build or not, so its members must agree.
cook.folded-column-types-differ: The consecutive column name rules are applied, but the column types do not match each other. (The type of {Index} must be {Type}.
recipe.member-case-unknown: The `{Target}` target sets `MemberCase` to `{Value}`. It takes `pascal`, `camel`, `snake` or `upper-snake`, or nothing at all to keep the spelling this language normally uses.
recipe.template-unknown: There is no starting recipe called `{Template}`. Use one of: {Known} - or leave --template off for one holding every setting at its default.
recipe.target-side-unknown: Recipe section `{Section}` has TargetSide `{Value}`, which is not recognized. Use "c" for client, "s" for server, or "cs" (the default) for both.
recipe.string-list-expected: Expected a string or an array of strings, and found {Found}. (at {Path})
recipe.layout-option-unknown: Recipe `{Section}` sets `LayoutOptions.{Key}`, which the `{Layout}` layout does not read. It takes: {Known}.
recipe.section-could-not-be-read: Recipe `{Section}` sets up target `{Target}`, but could not be read: {Detail}
recipe.target-entry-has-no-type: Recipe `Targets[{Index}]` has no `Type`, so there is nothing to say which target it configures. Use one of: {Known}.
recipe.target-unknown: Recipe `Targets[{Index}]` names target `{Target}`, which does not exist. Use one of: {Known}.
recipe.variables-not-set:
Recipe `{Filename}` refers to environment variables that are not set:{Listed}
Values are read from the environment so that a recipe can be committed in full, and so that one recipe can describe more than one environment. An unset variable is an error rather than an empty substitution, which would fail later and less clearly.
recipe.time-zone-unknown: {Subject} is `{Value}`, which is not a time zone this machine knows. A zone is named as `Asia/Seoul` or `Korea Standard Time`, and an offset is written `+09:00` for sheets whose authors keep one offset all year.
recipe.time-zone-unknown-with-suggestion: {Subject} is `{Value}`, which is not a time zone this machine knows. Did you mean {Suggestions}? A zone is named as `Asia/Seoul` or `Korea Standard Time`, and an offset is written `+09:00` for sheets whose authors keep one offset all year.
recipe.time-zone-data-unreadable: {Subject} is `{Value}`, and this machine's time zone data for it cannot be read. ({Detail})
recipe.time-zone-not-an-offset: {Subject} is `{Value}`, which is not an offset from UTC. An offset is written `+09:00`, `-05:30`, `+0900` or `+09`, and `Z` is UTC itself. A region's name works too, as `Asia/Seoul`.
recipe.time-zone-offset-too-large: {Subject} is `{Value}`, which is further from UTC than any place on earth. Offsets run from `-14:00` to `+14:00`.
cook.validation-failed: The workbook did not pass validation.
run.target-side-unknown: --target-side `{Value}` is not recognized. Use `client`, `server`, or `both` (the default).
run.validate-only-with-force-output: `--validate-only` and `--force-output` ask for opposite things: one stops before any output, the other insists every output entry runs. Pass one.
run.environment-named-twice: `--env {Asked}` was given while {Variable} is already set to `{Inherited}`. They label the same run and decide the same paths, so one of them is wrong. Clear the variable, or pass the environment it names.
run.environment-name-illegal: {Described} is not an environment name. This word goes into the paths a recipe builds with `${{{Variable}}}`, so it is limited to letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` - anything else would write the output somewhere the recipe does not describe.
cook.naming-consequence-splits: These do not normalize to one name, so the generated code carries a separate member for each spelling and every consumer has to know which one it is reading.
cook.naming-consequence-same: These normalize to the same name, so the generated code is unaffected - but the sheets disagree, and the next spelling of it may not be.
cook.naming-spelling-violation: {Said} is not spelled in `{Spelling}` case, which this recipe declares for {Kinds}. Write it as `{Wanted}`.
cook.naming-spelling-violation-in-level: {Said} has a level, `{Level}`, that is not spelled in `{Spelling}` case, which this recipe declares for {Kinds}. Write it as `{Wanted}`.
cook.naming-consecutive-underscores: {Said} holds two or more underscores in a row. A run of them reads as one word boundary, so this name and `{Collapsed}` both reach the generated code as `{Normalized}` - the difference is not carried anywhere. Write it as `{Collapsed}`.
cook.naming-consecutive-underscores-in-l: {Said} has a level, `{Level}`, holding two or more underscores in a row. A run of them reads as one word boundary, so this name and `{Collapsed}` both reach the generated code as `{Normalized}` - the difference is not carried anywhere. Write it as `{Collapsed}`.
cook.naming-spelling-conflict: {Subject} is written {Count} ways: {Spellings}. {Consequence} Settle on `{Recommended}` and rewrite the other {Places}.
cook.asset-file-missing: `{Table}.{Field}` names `{Name}`, and no file of that name is in the configured folders.
cook.asset-file-missing-for-kind: `{Table}.{Field}` names `{Name}`, and no file of that name is in the folders for kind `{Kind}`.
cook.known-problem-entry-incomplete: `Validation.KnownProblems` entry {Entry} needs both `At` and `Reason`. An entry without a place covers everything, and one without a reason is a switch rather than a note.
cook.known-problem-matched-nothing: `Validation.KnownProblems` names `{At}`, and nothing was reported there. Either it is fixed or the place is wrong; both are reasons to take the entry out. (`{Reason}`)
cook.known-problem-count-grew: `Validation.KnownProblems` says `{At}` accounts for {Expected} report(s) and it accounts for {Found}. Something new is wrong there, so the entry no longer says what is known. (`{Reason}`)
cook.known-problem-count-shrank: `Validation.KnownProblems` says `{At}` accounts for {Expected} report(s) and it accounts for {Found}. Some of it is fixed, so the entry no longer says what is known. (`{Reason}`)
cook.log-cache-seal-unwritable: The build cache could not be written to `{Path}`: {Detail}. This run's output is complete; the next one will convert everything.
cook.log-referenced-tables-unchecked:
`{Table}.{Field}` says its value is a row of `{Missing}`, which this build does not contain. The column is not checked.
    at {At}
recipe.report-open-unknown: `Report.OpenInBrowser` is `{Written}`, which is not one of `never`, `problems` or `always`.
report.outcome-nothing-to-do: Nothing had changed, so nothing was produced.
report.outcome-stopped: The conversion stopped. The data broke a rule.
report.open-in-sheet: Open this cell in the sheet
report.truncated: {Shown} of {Total} reports are on this page. Every one of them is in {File}.
report.uncompared: There is no earlier report to compare with, so nothing here is marked new.
report.defect-note: This is a defect in tabbit rather than a problem with the data or the recipe. Please report it with the call stack below.
